proposal:
SCOPE. Nothing was executed; every trace is by hand from the supplied code. No all-CNF bound is claimed.

1. AUDIT OF THE PINNED CODE.
(a) compression._verify_certificate rebuilds blocks from every original clause, confines each used form to its block mask, compares all 2^w local points and checks every entry of P*L=I. That yields F(x)=Q(Px) and surjectivity. I find no soundness defect, and every skip falls back.
(b) Exact-support blindness. In Neon58's quotient all 48 clauses have distinct supports, so every block has one forbidden point. On the direct form compress_root stops at all_variables_in_odd_blocks and probe at no_clauses_removed. Yet one side's 16 negative clauses jointly forbid 81 points of {0,1}^8, exactly g^-1(1111) for g = four ORs. The obstruction is cross-block and nonlinear, not a missing GF(2) kernel.
(c) Cost. step is lru-cached on the raw restricted tuple, not on canon_plus's output, so one canonical state reached by different restrictions re-runs refute. In the trace of section 4, IALH runs three times on the same 36-clause state. Caching on the canonical state is answer-preserving.
(d) Cost. hull_rows calls SymPy HNF for every window. If a table contains a point together with all w single-flip neighbours, the difference lattice contains every unit vector and the output is necessarily empty. This O(w*|table|) pre-check is sound in any case, because it can only omit rows. Every window I traced in the non-refuted fixture states satisfies it. Memoising on (w, table bitmask) covers the rest. Pigeonhole's 1467 windows are the target.

2. RESTRICTED SOUND RULE: TWIN (unimplemented).
In a subsumption-reduced CNF F, literals x,y on distinct variables are OR-twins if (T1) a clause contains x iff it contains y; (T2) not-x OR C is a clause iff not-y OR C is; (T3) no clause contains both negations. Since (not-x OR C)(not-y OR C) == not-(x OR y) OR C, F(x,y,rest) = F'(x OR y, rest), where F' has clauses p OR D and not-p OR C. This is exact equivalence through a surjection with lift (x,y):=(p,0): one variable fewer, no wider clause, no extension variable. Negating literals gives the AND forms. Every nondegenerate two-input gate is XOR-type or AND/OR-type, so BLQ plus TWIN exhausts syntactic arity-2 quotients.
Claims with proof sketches only: twinhood is an equivalence on literals; a literal and its negation cannot both have twins; merging one class preserves the twinhood of others. Hence a unique fixpoint up to renaming in fewer than n rounds. Discovery sorts positive-occurrence lists and contexts C: at most w*L symbols per round, O(n*w*L*log L) index comparisons in total. The certificate is the class list, rechecked by the same sort. As I recall, this is the special case of bounded variable addition (Manthey, Heule, Biere) in which the matched grid covers all occurrences, so the pair is deleted instead of a definition being added.

3. NEON58 UNDER BLQ THEN TWIN (independent-test prediction). The 16-variable quotient has eight twin classes of size two, all visible in round one. Result: 8 variables, 18 clauses: one negative 4-clause per side and sixteen p_i OR q_j. On that formula the pinned residual solver finds no SCC merge, and the IALH window {p1..p4} has an empty UP table (any p_i=0 forces every q_j and falsifies the q-clause; all ones falsifies the p-clause). Predicted UNSAT, peak 0, one IALH call.

4. FINITE FINDING: PEAK 8 IS A NUMBERING ARTIFACT. The fixture is the direct four-pair family with pairs (1,2),(3,4),(5,6),(7,8) against (9,10),...,(15,16), ascending order. Hand trace of pinned v5: compression skipped (all_variables_in_odd_blocks); core UNKNOWN (no_clauses_removed); root IALH yields no rows; no DP step is size-nonincreasing (4 positive by 8 negative occurrences give 32 resolvents for 12 removed clauses). x1=1 leaves the 3-against-4-pair family T (36 clauses); x1=0 leaves R (40 clauses). All 92 and 102 windows (no truncation) contain a point with all its neighbours, so neither is refuted, and neither subsumes the other: layer 1 retains 2. At x2: T is unchanged, R|x2=1 equals T, and R|x2=0 collapses to the B-side core, refuted by an empty table: layer 2 retains 1. Layers 3 and 4 repeat this. x5=1 produces units and the same empty table; x5=0 is closed by accepted DP on 7, 8, 6 and then the B variables. Predicted layers [2,1,2,1,0], peak 2. So a static twin-adjacent quotient order already removes the growth without merging.

5. NOT HANDLED. (i) One extra clause containing a single twin member in an unmatched context destroys that class; 2k adversarial extras destroy all of them. Untouched classes still merge. (ii) Prime modules of arity three or more. Stress family MAJ-transversal: three triples per side, 18 variables, 27 width-6 negative clauses per side choosing a 2-subset of every triple, 81 width-4 positive clauses. Each triple factors through MAJ3, but TWIN finds nothing and BLQ skips. (iii) Pigeonhole has no twins (p_ij and p_ij' have different negative contexts); only 1(c),(d) touch its cost. (iv) Generic 3-CNF has no twins: this is a restricted result, not a SAT algorithm.
missing_theorem:
MT1 (should be provable; needs an independent proof and a Lean lemma comparable to the existing block-composition one): TWIN equivalence and lift; the equivalence-relation, polarity-exclusion and commutation claims; hence a unique normal form, O(n*w*L*log L) discovery and an equal-cost certificate check.

MT2 (open to me): arity-t clausal modules. Call G a clausal module with split {A, complement of A} of {0,1}^G if, for each context D, the union of forbidden G-subcubes over clauses gamma OR D' with D' inside D is empty, A, its complement, or everything. Needed: are clausal modules closed under union of overlapping members, so that the least clausal module containing a given pair is polynomially computable without an arity cap? Without this, discovery costs n^t. As I recall (Bioch), semantic module recognition for general CNF is coNP-hard, so a syntactic closure theorem is the only route.

MT3 (exact residual obstruction; I do not expect a polynomial version): a total-work bound for formulas that are TWIN-normal and BLQ-irreducible. Given MT1 the normal form is itself a polynomial reduction, so SAT restricted to TWIN-normal formulas stays NP-complete. Any polynomial bound there is P=NP. TWIN and BLQ only strip decomposable structure.

MT4 (finite to family): for every k, pinned v5 on the k-pair family with pair-adjacent order retains at most 2 states over O(k) layers. Traced by hand for k=4 only. For k>=6 the negative clauses exceed the IALH window width, so the argument must go through DP alone.
self_attack:
1. TWIN is syntactic and brittle. It answers Neon58 exactly, but that family already has linear-size resolution refutations and, per section 4, peak 2 under a good order. Success on it is no evidence about hard instances.
2. The confluence and commutation sketches are unchecked. Twins can be hidden by subsumed clauses, so the rule depends on canonical form, and simultaneous merging of several classes relies on the commutation claim.
3. Fixture risks. I classified windows by type and checked one representative each. A lattice row I missed in T or R would give peak 1. The layer list is less certain than the peak: if IALH refutes the 28-clause layer-3 state, the layers become [2,1,1,0]. About 13 IALH calls and roughly 1000 windows could approach the 20-second budget; a timeout would be inconclusive.
4. The claim that the observed peak 8 comes from the quotient's fresh numbering is an inference. I did not reconstruct the greedy basis order.
5. The HNF shortcut's equality with SymPy's output is argued from the code, not tested. The cache change alters counting statistics, though not answers.
6. The bounded-variable-addition and Bioch attributions are from memory.
7. Nothing here helps pigeonhole or any prime instance beyond constant factors.
mechanism_signature: TWIN: definition-free OR/AND twin-literal merge (exact quotient x OR y -> p, lift (p,0)), confluent, sort-based discovery, the arity-2 nonlinear complement of BLQ. Twin-adjacent ordering traced on the direct 4-pair family (peak 2). Canonical-state cache and full-lattice HNF shortcut for total work. Clausal-module closure as the open step. MAJ-transversal as the prime-module stress family.
delta_from_prior: From the summaries I have, 00066 added rectangle definitions, 00067 used lookahead ordering and cofactor classes, and 00068 identified the class with monotone dualization and proposed FK-ORDER. New here: a variable-reducing exact rule with no extension variables, a lift, a confluence claim and near-linear discovery; the gate-type argument that BLQ plus TWIN covers all syntactic arity-2 quotients; a hand trace showing the 4-pair family peaks at 2 under a static pair-adjacent order, so the measured 8 is plausibly a numbering artifact; two code-level cost findings not in 00068's list (step cache keyed before canonicalization, SymPy HNF on full-lattice tables); and the observation that MT1 makes TWIN-normal SAT NP-complete, which pins down the residual obstruction. If 00066's rectangles already delete the paired variables, the delta shrinks to the confluence and cost claims plus the trace.
